# Can I afford to buy this business?

> Free calculator for buying a small business: enter the asking price, SDE and financing and see DSCR, cash needed at close, owner take-home, the highest price that still clears a lender's coverage floor and what happens if earnings fall. Private, runs in your browser.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## What it checks

- DSCR = (SDE - your salary - capex reserve) / a year of loan payments, against your floor; warns under 1.25, the SBA 7(a) minimum for buying a business (SOP 50 10 8.1).
- A seller note on full standby pays nothing while the bank loan runs: out of the DSCR and out of year-one cash, with its later payment shown.
- SBA equity injection: 10% of total project cost, a standby seller note supplying at most half.
- Cash needed at close, take-home after debt and salary, maximum price at your floor, and a table for SDE 10-30% lower.
- Not modelled: the SBA guaranty fee, the quality-of-earnings rule, collateral, taxes. Confirm SBA rules with a lender.
